chapters.title: Meqabis Destroys Jerusalem
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 1

The Moabite against the Holy City

1About Meqabis, who came upon the Jews in Mesopotamia of Syria and killed them in their valleys, from the Jabbok as far as the region of Jerusalem, and destroyed the holy city.

2For they made an agreement together, from Samaria to the region of Jerusalem and all its borders, and killed with the edge of the sword until they left none but a few; for the Edomites, the Syrians and the Amalekites joined with Meqabis the Moabite, who destroyed the city of Jerusalem.

3When the sons of Israel sinned, God sent Meqabis the Moabite against them, and he killed them all with the sword.

4Because of this the enemies of God shouted against His holy city and joined together in their feasting.

5The Edomites and the foreigners made an agreement and began to take vengeance on the city of God; for He Himself had sent them, because the people had despised the word of God.

6This Meqabis, whose city was Ramath of Moab, rose up in power from his city and joined forces with those who were with him.

7They encamped in the valleys of Gilboa of Mesopotamia as far as Syria, to destroy the city of God. From there he asked the foreigners and the Amalekites to be with him at the feasting, and gave them much gold and silver, horses and chariots.

8They came together and besieged the city, and poured out the blood of those who lived in it like water.

9They made Jerusalem like a watchman's hut in a field of gourds. They did filth and dung in it and all that God does not delight in, deeds of robbery, and they defiled the city of God, which was full of righteousness and holiness.

10They made the bodies of Your servants food for the birds of the sky, and the flesh of Your righteous ones food for the beasts of the field.

11They oppressed the widow and the orphan and ripped out what was in the wombs of the pregnant women, until God, who tests the heart and the kidneys, was angry; for they acted without the fear of God, as Satan had taught them.

12They went back to their borders rejoicing in the evil they had done to the people of God, and took the captives and the plunder they had seized from the holy city.

13When they came back to their dwellings, they held joy and merriment and feasting.

Notes

  • The text — the Ge'ez of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo printed Bible, and the verse numbers follow it. No other ancient text of the book is known. Like 1 Meqabyan, it is not the Greek 2 Maccabees. It opens with Meqabis, Maqābis, a king of Moab, a different man from the Maccabeus of 1 Meqabyan 2:1, whose name is written Maqābyos.

  • v1 "About Meqabis" — baʾənta za-rakabomu Maqābis, a title for what follows rather than a sentence.

  • vv4, 7, 13 "feasting" — māʿlet, the word for the celebration of v13. In v4 and v6 tasakātayu, joined together, is a word whose exact sense is uncertain.

  • v6 "Ramath of Moab" — Remāt za-Moʾāb, Meqabis's city, not otherwise known; Ramoth and Ramah are towns of Gilead and of Benjamin.

  • v8 "poured out the blood of those who lived in it like water" — They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem (Psalm 79:3).

  • v9 "like a watchman's hut in a field of gourds" — ləgata ʿāqābe qamḥ. The daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, like a lodge in a cucumber field, like a besieged city (Isaiah 1:8).

  • v10 "the bodies of Your servants food for the birds of the sky" — Psalm 79:2, word for word: They have given the bodies of Your servants to the birds of the heavens for food, the flesh of Your faithful to the beasts of the earth. The sudden Your is the psalm's.

  • v11 "ripped out what was in the wombs of the pregnant women" — the cruelty foretold of Hazael (2 Kings 8:12) and condemned in the Ammonites (Amos 1:13).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Word to Meqabis
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 2

Rejoice a Little

1Thus the prophet whom they call the Seer said to him: "Rejoice now a little, in the light of an hour; but God, the Holy One of Israel, will take vengeance on you, because you showed no regard.

2You say, 'My horses are swift runners, and so I will escape by flight.'

3But I will bring those who pursue you, running swifter than eagles, and you will not escape the trial and the wrath of God that is on you.

4Do you say, 'I will put on iron, and the shot of the bow and the thrust of the spear will not harm me, and so too with my coat of iron,' and that I will not take vengeance on you?" says God, the Holy One of Israel. "But I will bring an evil sickness into your heart, worse than the shot of the bow and the thrust of the spear, a sickness of sores and boils.

5I will bring an evil sickness into your heart, and you will look for one to help you and not find one, for you have kindled My wrath; and you will not escape from My hand until I wipe out the memory of you from the earth.

6You will know Me, that I am God your Creator, when I do this thing quickly, in the twinkling of an eye; for you stiffened your neck and lifted your head over My city. You are like grass before the wind, which fire eats before My eyes, and like ashes that the winds and the storm carry from the face of the earth; so are you before Me.

7For you have kindled My wrath and did not know your Creator; I too will not spare anything of yours, and I will leave none of yours on all your mountains.

8Now repent of all the evil you have done. If you repent and humble yourself before God with tears and weeping, and ask Him with a pure heart, God will pass over your sin in all you have sinned before Him."

Meqabis Repents

9At that time Meqabis wept before God for his sin and put on ashes, for God was angry with him.

10He knew that God does not delay the evil He has spoken through the mouth of His prophet; for His eyes are watchful and do not sleep, His ears are open and are not deaf, the word He has spoken does not lie, and He does it at once, in the twinkling of an eye.

11He threw off his clothes and put on sackcloth of hair, put ashes on his head, and wept and cried out before God his God for the evil he had done.

Notes

  • v1 "the prophet whom they call the Seer" — nabiy raʿāy za-yəbələwwo. The prophet is not named. Formerly in Israel… he who is now called a prophet was formerly called a seer (1 Samuel 9:9).

  • vv2–3 "My horses are swift runners… swifter than eagles" — You said, "No! We will flee upon horses"; therefore you shall flee away; and, "We will ride upon swift steeds"; therefore your pursuers shall be swift (Isaiah 30:16); Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles in the heavens (Lamentations 4:19).

  • v6 "like grass before the wind… like ashes that the winds carry" — like the chaff that the wind drives away (Psalm 1:4); O my God, make them like whirling dust, like chaff before the wind. As fire consumes the forest… (Psalm 83:13–14).

  • v10 "His eyes are watchful and do not sleep" — He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep (Psalm 121:4).

  • v11 "put on sackcloth… ashes on his head" — the king of Nineveh, at Jonah's word: he arose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes (Jonah 3:6).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Repentance of Meqabis
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 3

In the Pit

1The prophet spoke to him, for Ramath of Moab is near Syria.

2Meqabis dug a pit in the ground and went into it up to his neck, and wept bitterly and repented of the sin he had done before God.

3Thus God said to the prophet in the land of Judah: "Go back to the land of Ramath, to Meqabis the ruler of Moab, and say: Thus says God: It was not you who did this. Do not say, 'By the strength of my might and with my army I destroyed the holy city.' I am God, your Lord; by My own will I sent you to destroy My city,

4for she provoked Me with all her greed, her fornication and her deceit.

5I disregarded her and gave her into your hand. It was not for your sake; yet you stiffened your neck and said, 'I trampled the city by the strength of my hand.' Now, because of your children whom you fathered, God has passed over your sin.

6Now repent with all your heart and be steadfast, and do not be two-faced; for the two-faced do not hold firm in repentance.

7Blessed are those who repent with all their heart and do not turn back to robbery and sin in anything they have repented of their evil.

8They hold firm with weeping and tears, with much asking and with bowing down to God who created them; for He says to those who repent, 'You who went astray and then repented, you are Mine.'

9To the proud man too, after he went astray, when he returned to Him in repentance, He said: 'Because of your dismay and your fear I will pass over your sin; for I am God your Lord, who visits the sin of the father on the children to the third and fourth generation, and to those who love Me and keep My commandment I show mercy to the [number lost] generation.'

10Now, because of these children you fathered, I will keep My covenant with you, and accept the repentance you have made for the evil of your deeds," says God, the Holy One of Israel, who rules all.

Meqabis and the Prophet

11At that time he came out of the pit and bowed down to the prophet, saying, "May God do so and more to me if I part from you! But do with me whatever you wish. For I provoked God and did not walk in His commandment, as my fathers did not; we have no law, and you yourself know that we worship idols as our fathers taught us.

12As for me, until now I had not heard the word of the prophets of God; for I am a sinner who walked in my sin, in the pride of my heart and the stiffness of my neck, who provoked the commandment of God and did not walk in the commandment and the judgment He commanded me."

13The prophet answered him, "I know that your repentance has now been accepted, for before you there has been none of your kin who confessed his sin.

14From now on, leave the worship of idols and turn to the knowledge of God, so that your repentance may be true." Meqabis bowed down at the prophet's feet, and the prophet raised him up and commanded him every good deed that is fitting.

15He did as God commanded him, and went back to his house.

The Children of the Captivity

16Meqabis set his soul right, and removed from his house all divination and idols, sorcerers, sinners and soothsayers.

17The children of the captives whom he had brought from Jerusalem he questioned evening and morning about all the commandment of God, His law and His ordinance, as their fathers kept them.

18He appointed wise men from the children of the captivity in his house.

19Again, from the young ones, from their wise men, he appointed attendants in his bedchamber to keep his young children, their companions, and to teach them the way of God, as the sons of Israel did His law and His ordinance, His judgment and His justice; and about all the sacred places that the Moabites held sacred he would hear from the children of the captivity.

20He would abolish their sacred places, all their divinations, all their idols, all their altars of drink offering and their altars of sacrifice, the sacrifices from their fat beasts, the choice of his flocks and the young goats that he used to sacrifice to his gods evening and morning.

21For he had sacrificed to them and served them in every work, at noon and at every hour; he had asked them and trusted them and done their will in all that his gods, the deceivers, told him.

22He had not departed from their word in all they told him, for it seemed to him that they had saved him in everything.

23But Meqabis left their way.

The Way of Israel

24Once he heard the word of the Seer whom they call the prophet, he made his way good in repentance, and all his house made their way good, more than the sons of Israel in those days. For the sons of Israel provoke Him at one time, and at the time He punishes them they know Him and cry out to God.

25When He sees that they are brought low under the hands of those who afflict them, and they groan before Him, on that day He has mercy on them, remembering the covenant of their fathers when they cry out to Him, for the sake of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob their fathers.

26When He has saved them, they forget the One who saved them and go back to the worship of idols.

27On that day He sends against them nations who afflict them. When these have afflicted them and made them suffer, they cry out to God; at that time He has mercy and compassion on them, for He loves them, for they are the work of His hands.

28Again, when He bears with them, they go back to provoking Him with the worship of the idols around them and the evil work of their hands.

29He too raises up against them the people of the foreigners, Moab, Midian, Syria and Egypt; and they weep and cry out when their enemies have defeated them, made them suffer, made them serve and enslaved them. Then He raises up judges for them, to save them.

Notes

  • v2 "dug a pit… up to his neck" — the book's own picture of his repentance; v11 brings him out.

  • vv3–5 "It was not you who did this… by My own will I sent you to destroy My city" — Isaiah on Assyria: Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger… Against a godless nation I send him… For he says: "By the strength of my hand I have done it"… Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it? (Isaiah 10:5–6, 13, 15).

  • v5 "I trampled the city" — the Ge'ez has rodkəwwā, read as ragaṣkəwwā, I trampled it.

  • v6 "do not be two-faced" — nəfuq, a hypocrite. A double-minded man, unstable in all his ways (James 1:8).

  • v9 "to the third and fourth generation… mercy to the [number lost] generation" — the ten words: visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate Me, but showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love Me (Exodus 20:5–6). The Ge'ez has )), a numeral lost in the conversion of the text.

  • v10 "the repentance you have made" — the Ge'ez has za-gabarku, that I made, read as za-gabarka.

  • v11 "May God do so and more to me" — kamaz wa-kamaz la-yərassayani ʾƎgziʾabəḥer, the oath of Ruth: May the LORD do so to me and more also if anything but death parts me from you (Ruth 1:17).

  • vv24–29 the round of Israel — told as in 1 Meqabyan 28:17–35: sin, oppression, crying out, a savior, and sin again (Judges 2:11–19).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Meqabis Keeps the Law
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 4

The Judges

1Some were in the days of Hoshea,

2some in the days of Gideon,

3some in the days of Samson, Barak, Deborah and Judith. Whether by women or by men, He raises up judges for them, to save them from those who afflict them and from the hand of all their enemies,

4as God wills to save them from those who afflict them.

5They rejoice greatly in all the good He has done them, in the produce of their land and the increase of their cattle, and in all the flocks in the field and in the wilderness.

6He blesses their cattle and their plants, and all they hold, at home and in the wilderness He blesses for them, and does not let their cattle grow few; for He watches over them with His eyes and loves them greatly, for they are the generation of the righteous.

7But when they themselves become evil in their deeds, He gives them into the hand of their enemies.

8When He kills them, then they seek Him, and turn and rise early to seek God their Creator.

9When they turn with all their heart, He forgives them and does not remember their former offense; for He knows them, that they are flesh and blood, and have in them the misleading thoughts of this world and of the demons.

Meqabis Keeps the Law

10Once Meqabis heard this word, which God had established on His holy mountain, he strove in repentance.

11He did not cease to do what he had seen and heard of this word, and of all the good that the sons of Israel do, for God had compassion on them; when God punished them because they transgressed His commandment, they wept and cried out, and again He had compassion on them, and they kept His commandment.

12So too Meqabis set his ways straight, kept His commandment and walked in the commandment of God, the God of Israel.

13From the day he heard, in all that the sons of Israel boast of, he too boasted in keeping the commandment of God.

14He ordered his house and his children to walk in all the ways and commandments of God.

15What the Jews held forbidden he too held forbidden; the commandments the Jews keep, as he heard them, he too did; and the foods the Jews abstain from he abstained from, though he was of another people, a Moabite.

16He gave the tithes too, and the firstborn of his sheep, his cattle and his donkeys, and of all he acquired; and the sacrifices the Jews offer he too offered, facing toward Jerusalem:

17for vows and for sin, freewill offerings, the sacrifice of peace and the continual sacrifice,

18and the firstfruits. The drink offerings the Jews pour out he too poured out, and gave to the Levite who was appointed; all the Jews did, he did likewise, and the burning of incense.

19He made marānātā and milonāt, tables and tents, basins and ḫoṣādāt, beaten oil for the lamp of the holy place, and curtains, as they do in the holy of holies of Israel when they please God.

20For when they lived by His law and His ordinance, God did not disregard them or give them into the hand of their enemies; so Meqabis did well in all his ways.

21He prayed at all times to God, the God of Israel, to be his guide and not to cut him off from the assembly of Israel, whom He had chosen and who did His will.

22Again he prayed that God would give him seed in Zion and houses in Jerusalem, save him from the trial He had spoken through the mouth of the prophet, and accept his repentance in all he had repented of.

23He wept before God with tears, that He would not destroy his seed from the earth, and would keep him in his going out and his coming in.

A Just Ruler

24Of the nations of Moab under the hand of Meqabis, some were persuaded to believe, for their ruler walked a straight way. They saw his justice and did his will; they weighed the justice of their cities and the bounds of their country, and saw that what Meqabis did was more upright and far better.

25They came to him and heard the righteous judgment and the goodness of Meqabis.

26He had great wealth, male and female slaves, donkeys and camels; and he had horses that were clad in iron [words lost]

27From the time he worshiped God, when he went to war, none defeated him; he alone defeated.

28They came in the power of their gods to fight him and cursed him in the name of their gods, but none defeated him, for he had put his trust in God his God.

29He lived doing so, defeating his enemy and bringing nations under his hand.

30He took vengeance for the oppressed and did justice for the orphan.

31He took in widows and orphans and comforted them, fed the hungry from his own food, and clothed the naked from his own clothing.

32He rejoiced in his labor and the work of his hands, and gave from what he had without holding back, and gave tithes to the house of God. Doing this, Meqabis died in peace.

Notes

  • v1 "Hoshea" — Hośeʿ. In a list of judges and saviors it is likely Joshua, whose name was first Hoshea: Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua (Numbers 13:16).

  • v9 "He knows… that they are flesh and blood" — He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes and comes not again (Psalm 78:39); He knows our frame; He remembers that we are dust (Psalm 103:14).

  • v15 "though he was of another people, a Moabite" — the law said No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD (Deuteronomy 23:3); Ruth the Moabite said, Your people shall be my people, and your God my God (Ruth 1:16).

  • v16 "facing toward Jerusalem" — if they pray to the LORD toward the city that You have chosen (1 Kings 8:44); Daniel had windows in his upper chamber open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:10).

  • v19 the furnishings — marānātā, milonāt and ḫoṣādāt are not otherwise known. Pure beaten olive oil for the light, that a lamp may regularly be set up to burn (Exodus 27:20).

  • v22 "seed in Zion and houses in Jerusalem" — let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will surely separate me from His people"… I will give in My house and within My walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters (Isaiah 56:3, 5).

speech.text: 2 Meqabyan 4
The Judges
Some were in the days of Hoshea,
some in the days of Gideon,
some in the days of Samson, Barak, Deborah and Judith. Whether by women or by men, He raises up judges for them, to save them from those who afflict them and from the hand of all their enemies,
as God wills to save them from those who afflict them.
They rejoice greatly in all the good He has done them, in the produce of their land and the increase of their cattle, and in all the flocks in the field and in the wilderness.

He blesses their cattle and their plants, and all they hold, at home and in the wilderness He blesses for them, and does not let their cattle grow few; for He watches over them with His eyes and loves them greatly, for they are the generation of the righteous.
But when they themselves become evil in their deeds, He gives them into the hand of their enemies.
When He kills them, then they seek Him, and turn and rise early to seek God their Creator.

When they turn with all their heart, He forgives them and does not remember their former offense; for He knows them, that they are flesh and blood, and have in them the misleading thoughts of this world and of the demons.
Meqabis Keeps the Law
Once Meqabis heard this word, which God had established on His holy mountain, he strove in repentance.

He did not cease to do what he had seen and heard of this word, and of all the good that the sons of Israel do, for God had compassion on them; when God punished them because they transgressed His commandment, they wept and cried out, and again He had compassion on them, and they kept His commandment.
So too Meqabis set his ways straight, kept His commandment and walked in the commandment of God, the God of Israel.
From the day he heard, in all that the sons of Israel boast of, he too boasted in keeping the commandment of God.
He ordered his house and his children to walk in all the ways and commandments of God.

What the Jews held forbidden he too held forbidden; the commandments the Jews keep, as he heard them, he too did; and the foods the Jews abstain from he abstained from, though he was of another people, a Moabite.
He gave the tithes too, and the firstborn of his sheep, his cattle and his donkeys, and of all he acquired; and the sacrifices the Jews offer he too offered, facing toward Jerusalem:
for vows and for sin, freewill offerings, the sacrifice of peace and the continual sacrifice,
and the firstfruits. The drink offerings the Jews pour out he too poured out, and gave to the Levite who was appointed; all the Jews did, he did likewise, and the burning of incense.
He made marānātā and milonāt, tables and tents, basins and ḫoṣādāt, beaten oil for the lamp of the holy place, and curtains, as they do in the holy of holies of Israel when they please God.
For when they lived by His law and His ordinance, God did not disregard them or give them into the hand of their enemies; so Meqabis did well in all his ways.
He prayed at all times to God, the God of Israel, to be his guide and not to cut him off from the assembly of Israel, whom He had chosen and who did His will.

Again he prayed that God would give him seed in Zion and houses in Jerusalem, save him from the trial He had spoken through the mouth of the prophet, and accept his repentance in all he had repented of.
He wept before God with tears, that He would not destroy his seed from the earth, and would keep him in his going out and his coming in.
A Just Ruler

Of the nations of Moab under the hand of Meqabis, some were persuaded to believe, for their ruler walked a straight way. They saw his justice and did his will; they weighed the justice of their cities and the bounds of their country, and saw that what Meqabis did was more upright and far better.
They came to him and heard the righteous judgment and the goodness of Meqabis.
He had great wealth, male and female slaves, donkeys and camels; and he had horses that were clad in iron [words lost]
From the time he worshiped God, when he went to war, none defeated him; he alone defeated.
They came in the power of their gods to fight him and cursed him in the name of their gods, but none defeated him, for he had put his trust in God his God.
He lived doing so, defeating his enemy and bringing nations under his hand.
He took vengeance for the oppressed and did justice for the orphan.
He took in widows and orphans and comforted them, fed the hungry from his own food, and clothed the naked from his own clothing.
He rejoiced in his labor and the work of his hands, and gave from what he had without holding back, and gave tithes to the house of God. Doing this, Meqabis died in peace.

chapters.title: The Sons of Meqabis in Captivity
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 5

The Sons of Meqabis

1Meqabis left young children behind him, and they grew up as their father had ordered them. They kept the order of their house and all that was theirs, and did not make the poor, the orphan and the widow groan.

2They feared God and gave their goods as alms to the poor, and held to all their father had entrusted to them. They comforted the widow and the orphan, became father and mother to them, rescued them from the hand of their oppressors, and comforted them in all the trouble and grief that came upon them.

3They lived this way for five years.

Tsirutsaydan

4After that Tsirutsaydan, king of the Chaldeans, came and destroyed all their country, took the sons of Meqabis captive, and destroyed all their land.

5He plundered all their goods; and the Chaldeans seized the sons of Meqabis too and took them to their own country. They were worshipers of idols, who do not walk in the commandment and the judgment of God, but in all evil, fornication, uncleanness, greed and blasphemy, and do not remember their God.

6They eat everything that has died, blood, what a beast has eaten and what is torn, and all that God does not delight in; they have no law from all the commandments of righteousness written in the Law.

7They do not know God, that He is their Creator and their Savior, who brought them out of their mother's womb and fed them as was fitting.

8They have no law in judgment. They walk in robbery and wickedness, fornication and uncleanness, taking their father's wife and their mother's sister; they do every evil, taking their sisters and their kinswomen as wives, and they have no law.

9All their way is stumbling and darkness, uncleanness and fornication.

10But the sons of Meqabis kept themselves in all their abstinence, and did not eat what had died or what was torn, nor any of the uncleanness and sin of the Chaldeans; for their deeds are evil and many, not written in this book, which the sons of the ʾArabāmāyān do, sinners and rebels, heretics and perverse, full of uncleanness and wickedness.

11There is nothing in them that pleases God their Creator.

Bel Phegor

12Again, they worship an idol named Bel Phegor; they serve it and trust it as if it were God their Creator. For it is deaf and dumb and neither sees nor hears, for it is a carved image, the work of men's hands, which the smith cast of gold and silver, the work of the sons of men, with no understanding and no breath.

13It does not eat or drink,

14does not kill or make alive,

15does not plant or pluck up,

16does no harm and does no good,

17does not make poor or make rich,

18does not punish or have mercy; it is only a snare to lead astray the foolish people of the Chaldeans.

Notes

  • v3 "five years" — the Ge'ez has the digit 5; in this text a larger number may have been cut to a digit (1 Meqabyan 1:21).

  • v4 "Tsirutsaydan, king of the Chaldeans" — the persecutor of 1 Meqabyan 1–5, whose soldiers' fame reached all the land of Moab and the Chaldeans (1 Meqabyan 2:10).

  • v6 "They eat everything that has died" — the Ge'ez has wa-ʾi-yəballəʿu, and they do not eat, which the rest of the verse and v10 contradict; the negative is read as a slip.

  • v8 "taking their father's wife and their mother's sister" — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife… You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister (Leviticus 18:8, 13).

  • v10 "the sons of Meqabis kept themselves" — like Daniel in Babylon: Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's food (Daniel 1:8). ʾArabāmāyān is a people not otherwise known.

  • v12 "Bel Phegor" — Bəʾel Fegor, the Baal of Peor: Israel yoked himself to Baal of Peor. And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel (Numbers 25:3).

  • vv12–18 "deaf and dumb… does not eat or drink" — Their idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands. They have mouths, but do not speak; eyes, but do not see (Psalm 115:4–7); compare 1 Meqabyan 4:22.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Sons of Meqabis Burned
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 6

False Priests

1The proud Tsirutsaydan, the enemy of God, made false priests, deceivers for his gods.

2They sacrificed to them and poured out drink offerings to them,

3and he thought that the gods were the ones who ate and drank.

4He gave them cattle and sheep, fattened beasts and young goats, and they sacrificed evening and morning, and he ate of that unclean sacrifice.

5Not only did they do this themselves, but they enticed others too and compelled them to sacrifice to their gods.

The Sons of Meqabis Refuse

6When those deceivers saw the sons of Meqabis, that they were good and worshiped God their Creator, they wanted to lead them astray, so that they would sacrifice and eat of that unclean sacrifice. But these blessed men refused them.

7They could not make them say yes, for they kept the commandment of their father, held firm in doing good, and feared God greatly.

8Then they reviled them, spoke against them and wronged them,

9and told King Tsirutsaydan that they refused to bow down and sacrifice to his gods.

10Because of this the king was angry and grieved. He ordered them brought; they brought them and stood them before him, and he said to them, "Sacrifice and bow down to my gods."

11They answered him, "We will not yield to you in this, and we will not sacrifice to your unclean gods."

12He threatened them in many ways but could not overcome them, for they had made their hearts firm toward God.

13He kindled a fire and threw them in, and they gave up their souls to God.

They Appear to the King

14They appeared to him alive after their death, holding drawn swords, while he slept on his royal bed at night, and he was very afraid.

15He said to them, "What shall I do for you, my lords? Help me, and do not take my life, and I will do all you command me." They frightened him greatly.

16They told him all that was fitting, saying, "Remember that God is your Creator. There is One who will overthrow you from this pride of yours and bring you down to Gehenna below, with the devil your father; and there you will complete all your punishment, as you burned us with fire, though we had done you no wrong, while we worshiped God our Creator and bowed down to Him in the fear of God.

17For He is the Creator of all, who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that is in it,

18the sun and the moon and the stars and every creature that God Himself created.

19There is no other god besides Him in heaven above or on the earth below, who can do all, and nothing is too hard for Him, who kills and makes alive, who punishes and has mercy.

20No one escapes from His hand, for He is the ruler of heaven and earth.

21Of all He created, none transgresses His commandment but you, the wicked, and the wicked like you, whose hearts your father Satan has blinded; you and your gods will go down together into Gehenna, where there is no way out forever.

22For it is not you alone who do this, but Satan your teacher, who taught you this evil deed, to do us harm.

23You did not know God your Creator, and you make yourself out to be like God your Creator.

24You exalt yourself in the work of your hands and in your idols, until God brings you low and takes you down to the depths of Gehenna, and takes vengeance on you for all the offense and sin you have done on the earth.

Notes

  • vv1–4 the priests and the sacrifice — the deceit of Tsirutsaydan's priests in 1 Meqabyan 1:7–9, and of the priests of Bel in the Greek Daniel (Daniel 14:15).

  • v13 "He kindled a fire and threw them in" — the death of the sons of Maccabeus in 1 Meqabyan 3:35–37, under the same king. The book does not name these sons or say how many they were.

  • vv14–15 "They appeared to him alive… holding drawn swords" — as the five martyrs appeared to him in 1 Meqabyan 4:8–10.

  • v19 "who kills and makes alive" — I kill and I make alive (Deuteronomy 32:39).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Better Than You Are the Beasts
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 7

Woe to You

1"Woe to you, you and those like you, who do not know God who created you, and do not know His commandment and His word! For you will repent where repentance does no good, when you are punished in the torment of Sheol.

2There is no way out of it for you forever, you and your gods, and those who sacrifice and bow down to them as if they were God your Creator, to things that have no soul and no breath, that do not avenge those who harm them or do good to those who do good to them.

3For they are the work of men's hands, in which Satan speaks to lead astray the hearts of fools like you, to bring you down to the Gehenna of fire, you and your deceiving gods and the demons you obey.

4For you do not know that they profit you nothing; you sin and go astray.

5The cattle that God created for your food are better than you, and the beasts too, and the dogs; for they have no second judgment, only one death.

6But you will die and be judged a second time, in the terror of Gehenna, where there is no way out forever."

The Bodies Hidden

7When they had said this, they passed on and vanished from him.

8Tsirutsaydan was in great fear and trembling, and it did not leave him until morning.

9After that he went to where he had thrown the bodies of the righteous, and did not find them. He wanted to bury them and could not, for God had hidden them, so that their bodies could not be found.

Notes

  • v1 "you will repent where repentance does no good… the torment of Sheol" — the rich man in Hades, being in torment, who asks too late for his brothers to be warned (Luke 16:23–28).

  • vv5–6 "only one death… judged a second time" — This is the second death, the lake of fire (Revelation 20:14).

  • v9 "God had hidden them, so that their bodies could not be found" — of Moses: He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab… but no one knows the place of his burial to this day (Deuteronomy 34:6).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Iron Kingdom
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 8

Tsirutsaydan's Pride

1He went on in pride and in the deceit of his heart.

2He went around the regions of the nations around him; for it was said of his kingdom that it was like the iron that Daniel the prophet saw.

3He walks in all folly, evil and tumult.

4As we have told before, it crushes, breaks in pieces and devours,

5and what is left it tramples with its feet; for he is an oppressor, like his father the devil, stiff of neck.

6He does not know God, that He is his Creator, he who says, "My days have become like the days of heaven."

7He thinks in his heart that the sun rises from him.

8He rises up in Gad and settles in the land of Zebulun, raises war in Macedonia, takes food from Samaria, and they give him tribute from Syria.

9He settles as far as the region of Kedar and spreads as far as Sidon, imposes labor in Achaia, raises his neck as far as the river Takkaze, and turns back and spreads his rule as far as the sea of India.

10So he raises his neck to heaven.

11He does not humble himself, but goes in all evil and arrogance.

12All his way is in stumbling and darkness, arrogance and rebellion, destruction and the shedding of blood.

13All the ways that God hates he follows, as Sablanyos, his teacher of evil, taught him wickedness and robbery; he makes the orphan groan and has no pity on the poor.

14The kings of the nations he brought under his hand and killed.

15The commanders of the enemy he judged, and many nations he subdued and made them serve as he wished.

16He did not stop, and there was none he did not plunder, from the sea of Tarshish to the sea of Jericho.

17He bows down to idols and eats what has died, blood, what is torn and what is sacrificed to the gods. There is no justice in him, but in all his ways there is lawlessness, wrath, anger and tumult; for he became a terror to the nations under his hand, and he forced them to work as he wished.

18There is no fear of God before their eyes, for all that pleases him he does before Him, and he walks in deceit before God his Creator.

19He does not regard Him as his God; and God will repay him as he has done evil to his neighbor, on the day He seizes him in His wrath.

God Repays the Proud

20He will take vengeance on him in its time, as He uprooted the sinners who were before them; for He has said, "I am God, who takes vengeance on the proud who do not walk in My commandment, and I will uproot their memory from the earth."

21The evil will be repaid as they did evil.

22But goodness from God will follow the doers of good.

23As Joshua destroyed the kings of Canaan at one time, the five kings in one cave, and by his prayer made the sun stand still at Gibeon so as to destroy their army, and killed at one time about [number lost]; for the sun stood in the middle of heaven until he had destroyed the army of the Canaanites, the Hivites, the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Jebusites. Their kings too he killed: he put their feet on their necks, killed them with the edge of the sword, and covered them with stones in the cave.

24So it overtakes those who provoked God with the evil of their deeds.

Notes

  • vv2–5 "like the iron that Daniel the prophet saw… crushes, breaks in pieces and devours" — a fourth kingdom, strong as iron, because iron breaks to pieces and shatters all things (Daniel 2:40); it devoured and broke in pieces and stamped what was left with its feet (Daniel 7:7, 19).

  • vv6–7 "My days have become like the days of heaven… the sun rises from him" — Nebuchadnezzar's boast in 1 Meqabyan 5:3, I am the one who makes the sun rise on the earth.

  • v9 "the river Takkaze… the sea of India" — Takkaze is the Tekezé, the great river of northern Ethiopia, flowing into the Nile; the king's reach runs from Kedar in Arabia to Ethiopia and India.

  • v13 "Sablanyos, his teacher of evil" — Sablānyos, the teacher of the wicked in 1 Meqabyan 13:3 and 17:3–5.

  • v16 "from the sea of Tarshish to the sea of Jericho" — the far west and the Dead Sea by Jericho.

  • v23 Joshua and the five kings — Sun, stand still at Gibeon… And the sun stopped in the midst of heaven (Joshua 10:12–13); the five kings hid in the cave at Makkedah, and Joshua's captains put their feet on the necks of these kings; he killed them, and they set large stones against the mouth of the cave (Joshua 10:16–27). The Ge'ez has 5 for the kings, and 2)) for those killed, a number lost in the conversion of the text.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

He will take vengeance on him in its time, as He uprooted the sinners who were before them; for He has said, "I am God, who takes vengeance on the proud who do not walk in My commandment, and I will uproot their memory from the earth."
The evil will be repaid as they did evil.
But goodness from God will follow the doers of good.

As Joshua destroyed the kings of Canaan at one time, the five kings in one cave, and by his prayer made the sun stand still at Gibeon so as to destroy their army, and killed at one time about [number lost]; for the sun stood in the middle of heaven until he had destroyed the army of the Canaanites, the Hivites, the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Jebusites. Their kings too he killed: he put their feet on their necks, killed them with the edge of the sword, and covered them with stones in the cave.
So it overtakes those who provoked God with the evil of their deeds.

chapters.title: The Broad Way and the Narrow
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 9

O Man, and Not God

1You too, O man, and not God, why do you exalt yourself, you who are a man today and tomorrow earth and ashes, and will become worms and maggots in your grave?

2Sheol will follow you and those who do your deeds; for your teacher Sablyanos brought on his own head the sin of all the world, because by his pride he led our father Adam astray.

3For he refused to bow down to the work of his God, exalting himself and stiffening his neck.

4You too, like your teacher, have refused to bow down to the Lord your God.

5You too walk as those before you walked, who did not know the Lord their God.

6He took vengeance on them, and they went down into Sheol for the evil of the deeds they did on the earth.

7You too, like them, will go down into Gehenna.

8Do you think you will escape from God's hand? For you have kindled His wrath and grown slack in the worship of God, who gave you authority over five kingdoms.

9He tested you, whether you would do His will or not. If you make your way good on the earth, God will make your ways good; all you put your hand to He will make good and bless for you, and He will subdue all your enemies and adversaries for you.

10You will rejoice in your going out and your coming in, in the fruit of your womb, your storehouses and your flocks. Wherever you point your fingers and whatever you think in your heart, all will obey you, for it is granted you by God to do so, to build and to plant and to pull down.

11But if you refuse to hear the word and the law of God and do not walk in His judgment, you have nowhere to escape from the hand of God, like all the rebels before you, who did not worship God in purity and did not trust in His upright judgment; for all His judgment is righteousness.

12Nothing is hidden from His eyes; all is uncovered and laid bare before Him.

13He holds the authority of kings and overthrows the thrones of the mighty.

14He lifts up the humble and raises the fallen.

15He sets the prisoners free and raises the dead; those whose flesh has decayed and become like dust He wakes when He wills, for the dew of mercy is from Him.

16Those who did evil He raises at that resurrection of judgment, for they provoked Him, and He takes vengeance on them.

17On earth too He destroys their seed, for they are rebels against the law and the ordinance of God.

The Two Ways

18Sinners do not want to be in the counsel of the righteous, for the way of the righteous is hard compared with the way of sinners.

19As high as heaven is above the earth, so far is the way of the righteous from the way of sinners.

20The way of sinners is the doing of robbery and wickedness, wrongdoing and fornication, perversity and greed, seizing others' goods, and drunkenness in wrongdoing,

21running to shed blood, ruining for nothing, making the orphan weep, eating what has died and blood, eating the flesh of swine and camel, and going in to a woman in her impurity or after childbirth, before she is cleansed.

22All these deeds of sinners are a broad way, the spread net of Satan, which leads to perdition and eternal judgment.

23But the way of the righteous is narrow and hard, and it leads to life: humility and gentleness, love and peace, fasting and prayer, purity of body, and keeping from foods that do no good, what has died and what is torn, and from fornication and going to another man's wife.

24They keep themselves from every filthy deed, from unclean foods not commanded in the law, and from the filthy deeds God does not delight in; for all this the sinners do.

25But the righteous turn away from all the evil ways that God does not delight in.

26He loves them, takes them into His keeping, and saves them from all their distress.

27But Satan makes the sinners his own, for they keep his law and his ordinance and all that he loves.

Notes

  • vv2–3 "he refused to bow down to the work of his God" — the devil's fall told in the Life of Adam and Eve: commanded to worship the image of God in Adam, he refused, saying that Adam was younger than he and below him (Life of Adam and Eve 13–14). Sablyanos is the teacher of evil of 1 Meqabyan 13:3 and 17:3–5.

  • v8 "authority over five kingdoms" — the Ge'ez has the digit 5; 1 Meqabyan 5:24 gives the king four kingdoms.

  • v10 "in your going out and your coming in, in the fruit of your womb" — Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb… Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out (Deuteronomy 28:4, 6).

  • v12 "all is uncovered and laid bare before Him" — no creature is hidden from His sight, but all are naked and exposed to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account (Hebrews 4:13).

  • vv13–15 "overthrows the thrones of the mighty… sets the prisoners free" — He has brought down the mighty from their thrones and exalted those of humble estate (Luke 1:52); the LORD sets the prisoners free; the LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD lifts up those who are bowed down (Psalm 146:7–8). The dew of mercy: your dew is a dew of light, and the earth will give birth to the dead (Isaiah 26:19).

  • vv18–19 "the counsel of the righteous… As high as heaven is above the earth" — Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked (Psalm 1:1); as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways (Isaiah 55:9).

  • v21 "the flesh of swine and camel… a woman in her impurity or after childbirth" — the law forbids the camel and the pig (Leviticus 11:4, 7), and a man coming near a woman while she is in her menstrual uncleanness (18:19), or before the days of her purifying after childbirth are complete (12:2–4).

  • vv22–23 "a broad way… narrow and hard, and it leads to life" — the gate is wide and the way is easy that leads to destruction… the gate is narrow and the way is hard that leads to life (Matthew 7:13–14).

chapters.title: Balaam and the Fall of Jerusalem
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 10

Balak and Balaam

1You too, kings and rulers, do not walk in his way, but fear God, who created you and has kept you until now.

2Walk in the commandment and the judgment of God, who rules all.

3For Balak son of Zippor, when the sons of Israel came toward Amalek to inherit the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites and the Perizzites,

4said to Balaam, "Come, curse them for me; for whom you curse is cursed, and whom you bless is blessed. I will give you much gold and silver to honor you, if you curse them for me."

5Balaam came, hoping for the reward of his wrongdoing, and Balak son of Zippor showed him where the sons of Israel were encamped.

6He practiced divination and offered sacrifice, slaughtering sheep and cattle from the fattest of them, and wanted to curse the sons of Israel.

7But God did not want him to curse them, and by His word He turned the curse into a blessing.

8Balaam said, "Those who bless you shall be blessed, and those who curse you shall be cursed; for you are a people God has chosen, and you are the dwelling of the Beloved who comes from on high."

9Then Balak son of Zippor grieved and was angry and enraged, because Balaam had blessed them, blessed them before him; and he ordered him to curse them.

10Balaam said to him, "I will not curse those whom God has blessed, for the people God has chosen have come into this land."

11Balak son of Zippor said to Balaam, "I wanted you to curse them for me, and you did not curse them; you have blessed them, blessed them before me. I would have given you my house full of gold and silver, if you had said, 'Give me,' and cursed them for me. But you have blessed them, blessed them, and have not done well by me, and I will not do well by you."

12Balaam said, "I cannot disregard and transgress the word of God; the word God puts in my mouth, that is what I speak.

13I do not prize goods above my soul; for if I loved goods, God would be angry with me, for I am not to curse a blessed people.

14For God said to Jacob their father, 'Those who bless you, let them be blessed, and those who curse you, let them be cursed'; for everyone who blesses you is blessed,

15and whoever curses you without justice is cursed." Make your deeds and your way good, so that God may be pleased with you.

Jerusalem Plowed

16Do not be like the first people, who provoked God with their evil, and He disregarded them. Some He wiped out with the waters of the flood,

17and some He destroyed by the hand of their enemies. He brought an enemy, an evil people, who made them suffer and took their kings captive, with their prophets and their Levites,

18brought them to a foreign country they did not know, took them captive, plundered them, punished them and ruined their country.

19They made Jerusalem like a plowed field, for they pulled down the ramparts and the wall of the holy city.

20The priests were taken captive, the law was abolished, and the men fell by the spear.

21The widows were taken captive and did not weep for their husbands who had died, for they themselves were taken captive and were on their way.

22The children wept, the old were put to shame, and the enemy had no pity on the face of the old man and the gray-haired,

23nor on those in the sabsab, nor on the virgins. They ruined all they found in their cities and carried them off to a foreign country they did not know; for when God wills to be angry with His people, He first pulls down His sanctuary.

24Because of this, when God disregarded the sons of Israel, God made Jerusalem to be plowed like a field, for they always provoked their Creator.

25But He did not destroy them all at once, for He pitied them for their fathers' sake. It was not for their own sake that He pitied them, but because He loves their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who reigned in righteousness and walked before their Creator in uprightness.

26He made them a double honor, in heaven and on earth, and they won two kingdoms.

27So you too, kings and rulers who are in this passing world, remember those before you who walked in purity, so that they inherited the kingdom of heaven and their name was good from generation to generation.

28You too, so that your kingdom may stand upright and your name be good, like the good kings before you who pleased God by the beauty of their life.

Notes

  • vv3–15 Balak and Balaam — told from Numbers 22–24. Come now, curse this people for me… for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed (Numbers 22:6); Balaam loved gain from wrongdoing (2 Peter 2:15); the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you (Deuteronomy 23:5).

  • v8 "the dwelling of the Beloved who comes from on high" — the book's own words in Balaam's blessing. Numbers has Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you (Numbers 24:9), and Balaam's later oracle, a star shall come out of Jacob (24:17).

  • v14 "God said to Jacob their father" — the words are Isaac's to Jacob (Genesis 27:29), and God's to Abraham (Genesis 12:3).

  • vv19, 24 "Jerusalem like a plowed field" — Zion shall be plowed as a field; Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins (Micah 3:12, quoted in Jeremiah 26:18).

  • v21 "did not weep for their husbands" — their widows made no lamentation (Psalm 78:64).

  • v23 "the sabsab" — a word not otherwise known.

  • v26 "they won two kingdoms" — the Ge'ez has 2 mangəśta.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Moses and the Sons of Korah
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 11

The Gentleness of Moses

1Remember Moses the man of God, in his prayer and his humility. Though he saw what his people were, he was not angry and did not destroy them. For those who reviled him, his brother among them, and for those whom God wanted to destroy at once, he made atonement before God in gentleness, saying, "Have mercy, O God, on Your people, and do not disregard them, for Your people have sinned before You.

2As for me, Your sinful servant, have compassion on me, for I have sinned before You; and forgive them too, for You are merciful and compassionate."

3So he made atonement for those who reviled him.

4Because of this he was known as gentle.

5God loved him greatly, more than all the sons of the Levites, his brothers, and made him like God to them, for he also appointed the priests.

6Those who transgressed, the sons of Korah, God sank beneath the earth and brought down to Sheol alive, soul and body, with their tents and their cattle. Every word Moses spoke was done for him as for God, for he loved the Lord his God and did not transgress His commandment.

7So you too, if you do not transgress the commandment of God, God will do your will, be pleased with your word and keep your kingdom.

The Censers

8The sons of Korah and Asaph transgressed the commandment of Moses and murmured against him, because he told them, "Set your souls right before God."

9They said to him, "Are we not the sons of Levi, who do the work of the priesthood in the holy tent?"

10They took their censers to burn incense, and went and burned incense; but God did not accept their prayer. By the fire of their own censers they were burned and melted like wax that melts in fire, and nothing of them was left, not their bones or their clothes, only the bronze censers, which they brought into the house of God at God's command; for He said, "Their censers have become holy by the burning of their flesh."

11Because of this God said to Moses and Aaron, "Gather their censers into the tent, and let them be a covering for My house and for all I have ordained for it, from outside to inside."

12He made good the covering of the holy tent: the mercy seat and the ḫoṣādāt, the cherubim and the basins,

13the bowls, the carrying poles and the mawādəd, the court and the screens of the tent, the dishes, and the sacrifices they offered in the holy tent:

14the freewill offering, the sacrifice of salvation, the vow offering, the offering for sin and the sacrifice by His law.

15All He had commanded Moses to do in the holy tent, Moses commanded them.

The Dwelling of His Name

16They did not neglect to serve their God, so that His name would be praised among them in the tent of the law of the Lord their God, who promised to give them the inheritance of their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey, which He swore to Abraham.

17He made a covenant with Isaac and established a testimony for Jacob,

18and for Moses and Aaron in the tent of witness,

19and for Samuel and Elijah in Jerusalem, in the tent in the temple, where Solomon built, until it became the house of God, the resting place of the name of the Most High and the dwelling of the Holy One of Israel.

20For it is the place of asking and of the forgiveness of sin, where He appears to His priests who walk in gentleness,

21where He hears the prayer of those who do His will,

22where the law of God, the Holy One of Israel, is ordained,

23and where sacrifice and incense are burned for a soothing aroma to God, the Holy One of Israel.

24He speaks above the mercy seat in the holy tent, and the glory of God appears to His chosen ones, the sons of Jacob, and His holy ones who walk in the commandment and the judgment of God.

25But those who reproach Him will be like the sons of Korah, whom the earth swallowed; so too the sinners are bound to be cast into the judgment of burning fire, where there is no way out forever.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Have mercy, O God, on Your people… forgive them" — Moses after the calf: But now, if You will forgive their sin — but if not, please blot me out of Your book (Exodus 32:32). Those who reviled him, his brother among them: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses (Numbers 12:1), and Moses prayed for Miriam (12:13).

  • v4 "he was known as gentle" — Now the man Moses was very meek, more than all people who were on the face of the earth (Numbers 12:3).

  • v5 "made him like God to them" — you shall be as God to him (Exodus 4:16); I have made you like God to Pharaoh (Exodus 7:1).

  • vv6, 8–10 Korah — the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households… So they and all that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol (Numbers 16:32–33); fire came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men offering the incense (16:35). Numbers names Korah with Dathan and Abiram; the book names Asaph, a Levite singer of David's time (1 Chronicles 6:39).

  • vv10–11 "Their censers have become holy… let them be a covering" — the censers of these men who have sinned at the cost of their lives. Let them be made into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, for they offered them before the LORD, and they became holy (Numbers 16:38).

  • vv12–13 the furnishings — ḫoṣādāt (as in 4:19) and mawādəd are not otherwise known.

  • v24 "He speaks above the mercy seat" — There I will meet with you, and from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim… I will speak with you (Exodus 25:22).

chapters.title: The Death of Tsirutsaydan
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 12

Woe to the Mighty of Israel

1"Woe to you, mighty ones of Israel, who did not keep what I commanded you in the tent, and did not do My will, only your own will: pride and arrogance, fornication and greed, drunkenness and carousing and swearing falsely!

2Because of this My wrath will burn against you like stubble before the fire, like fire that burns the mountains, and like a stormy wind that lifts the fine dust from the earth and scatters it high in the air, where no trace of it is found.

3So I will destroy from before My face all who do evil," says God, the Holy One of Israel. Remember God, who rules all, and nothing is too hard for Him.

4He loves those who love Him, and forgives the sins and offenses of those who walk in His commandment. Do not be stubborn and dull of heart, unbelieving.

5Set your souls right before God and hold to Him, so that you may save your souls. "I will save you from the hand of your enemy on the day of your distress.

chapters.title: Better One Day in Paradise
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 13

What the Sons of Meqabis Knew

1But these five Maccabees, the sons of Meqabis, believed and gave themselves up to death, refusing to eat the sacrifice of idols,

2and gave themselves up to the fire, so as to be saved from the fire in heaven, knowing that this world passes away

3and that pleasure does not last forever. For they knew that the reproach of God is worse than the reproach of the sons of men, and the wrath of God worse than the wrath of the king.

4One day of rejoicing in the gardens of paradise is better than thousands of years of life on the earth; and better than long days is one hour of Your mercy, O Lord.

5What are the days of man? Do they not pass like a shadow, and like wax before the fire?

6But You, O Lord, live forever; Your years do not end, and Your remembrance is from generation to generation.

7All this and the like the sons of Meqabis thought; they chose, they chose to trust in God, and refused to eat the unclean sacrifice.

8Because of this they gave up their bodies to bear witness for God's sake, knowing that the dead will rise, and that there will be judgment after the resurrection.

Learn from These Five

9You who do not know and do not believe in the resurrection of the dead, learn now from these five good men of one family, who together gave themselves up to death, knowing that their latter life would be better than this earthly one that passes away.

10They saw that all passes away, and gave themselves up to death, so as to find praise from God because they believed in Him, did not bow down to idols, and did not eat the sacrifice of the dead and of uncleanness.

11Because of this, knowing that He would make them rejoice on the last day in soul and body, though they had wives and children, they did not regard the sweetness of this world or the bitterness of death, and gave themselves up to death, knowing that there will be a resurrection on the last day in soul and in body.

12They knew that those who kept the ordinance of God will reign in the world to come, from generation to generation and for long days, where there is no sickness or sorrow.

13Where there is no sickness or sorrow and no death, with the good kings and rulers who believed in the word of God, there they gave themselves up to death like wax in the fire, seeing in the thought of their hearts what is to come,

14and hoping that their faces would shine seven times brighter than the sun, and that they would be filled with His love at the resurrection of all, in soul and in body.

Notes

  • v1 "these five Maccabees" — the Ge'ez has the digit 5 (and again in v9). The sons of Meqabis burned by Tsirutsaydan in 6:13 were not counted there; the martyrs of 1 Meqabyan 2–4 were five as well.

  • v4 "One day of rejoicing in the gardens of paradise is better than thousands of years" — For a day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere (Psalm 84:10).

  • vv5–6 "like a shadow… like wax before the fire… Your years do not end" — his days are like a passing shadow (Psalm 144:4); as wax melts before fire (Psalm 68:2); You are the same, and Your years have no end (Psalm 102:27).

  • v10 "the sacrifice of the dead" — they yoked themselves to the Baal of Peor, and ate sacrifices offered to the dead (Psalm 106:28).

  • v14 "shine seven times brighter than the sun" — the light of the sun will be sevenfold (Isaiah 30:26); the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father (Matthew 13:43).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Those Who Deny the Resurrection
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 14

What They Say

1As for me, I grieve greatly, I am sorrowful, and my heart burns within me because of the Jews and the Samaritans, the Pharisees and the Sadducees, who do not believe in the resurrection of the dead. The Jews say, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die, and there we will see nothing."

2The Samaritans say, "Our flesh will not rise, for it becomes dust.

3If there is a resurrection, we believe in the resurrection of our souls; for the soul does not die even if the flesh dies. It is like the wind, which is not seen, and like the sound of thunder, of which no one says, 'Here it is,' and which does not appear.

4But our flesh is seen by all, and becomes ashes and dust; beasts eat it, and worms eat it in the grave.

5Those that ate it also become ashes, and no trace of them is found; they become like grass, and become ashes as though they had never been created.

6That is where the bodies that have decayed are found." Thus the Pharisees say: "We believe in the resurrection of the dead; but in heaven He will clothe the souls with another body, not the earthly one."

7Thus the Sadducees say: "Once our soul has gone out of our body we will not rise from the dead." They have no resurrection of the dead, neither for the soul nor for the body: "Once we have died, we will not rise."

8Because of this they are utterly foolish, and they grieve me, for they speak blasphemy against God and His glory.

9They have no hope of salvation, for they did not believe in God, who makes them righteous; they have no hope of salvation or of the resurrection of the dead.

The Rope of Sheol

10O blind Jew, do you think God a fool, who brought you from where you were not, and while you were spittle made you a man? Is it too hard for Him who sowed you to make your soul and your body sprout again in His image and His likeness?

11Do not think so; you will not escape from the hand of God. You will rise even if you do not wish it, and be judged even if you are not willing; for the rope of Sheol is on your neck, by which you will be seized on the day of your death.

12In your mother's womb that rope sprouts for you from the stock of Sheol, the rope they put on your neck; as you grow, so it grows.

13When you die they put it on your neck, and when they pull it, its stock draws them in.

14It pulls its branches, for all the sinners are held in it, like ropes on their necks.

15It draws all the souls of sinners from where they are, from the ends of heaven; so your rope pulls you, to bring your soul from where you are and return you to the river of Sheol.

16Your flesh too, after it has passed away, the dew of God's mercy will raise up sevenfold, like the body of our father Adam; and there you will be repaid as you have done offense and sin, according to your unbelief.

17Do not think that because you lead another astray and go astray yourself, you will stay in the grave in your error, saying, "There is no resurrection of the dead," so that people go astray from the commandment of God.

18Who will leave you in the dust and the earth? He will raise you up, to repay you according to the deeds you have done.

19Then they will come: your spirits from the winds, your dust from the earth, your flame from the fire,

20and the breath of life that was breathed into you, from the court of darkness,

21where it is shut in. But the souls of the righteous are kept in the garden, in joy.

22As for you, O Jew and Samaritan, Pharisee and Sadducee, until the time of your judgment you will be bound in darkness.

23Then you will see how God repays you according to your deeds, because your heart led you astray.

24You said to them, "The dead do not live; let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die"; and with your own voice, while you sit on the seat of Moses, you say, "There is no resurrection of the dead."

25Because of this you went astray, though you know the book of the Law and teach the words of the Scriptures; and you lead people astray. It would have been better for you not to teach and not to know

26the words of the Scriptures than to lead the people of God astray by your evil teaching and your useless word.

27You will be repaid according to your deeds and the fruit of your lips; for God shows no favor to persons, and those who teach good He repays from the good things He has prepared for those who love Him.

28You have nowhere to escape from the hand of Him who judges you; He will repay you according to your deeds, for you and those you taught will be judged together.

The Dead Will Rise

29I know that the dead will rise. Those who kept His commandment will rise, and standing will not be hard for them, for His commandment brings them out, as the earth brings out grass when the rain strikes it,

30as a green tree puts out leaves when the rain has watered the earth, and as it bears the fruit of wheat or a crop of grain, and its fruit cannot be held back when God is pleased.

31As a pregnant woman, when her labor comes, cannot hold her womb closed once she has heard the word of God, but gives birth at once, for the dew from God comes down on her,

32so the earth too, on the day, brings out those stored up in her; she cannot hold her womb closed once she has heard the word of God, but gives birth to them at once, for the dew from God comes down on her.

33The bodies gather in their places, where their corpses fell; the storehouses of the souls are opened, and the souls return into the bodies from which they went out before.

34At the blowing of the horn the dead will rise in the twinkling of an eye and stand before God, and He will repay them according to the work of their hands.

35Then you will see that you rise from the dead, and you will marvel at all the deeds you did on the earth, when you see them written before your eyes; and on that day you will repent where it does you no good.

36You will know that you rise from the dead and are repaid according to the deeds you have done.

Notes

  • v1 "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" — Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die (Isaiah 22:13), as Paul quotes it: If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink" (1 Corinthians 15:32).

  • vv6–7 the Pharisees and the Sadducees — the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all (Acts 23:8). Another body, not the earthly one: Paul, There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies (1 Corinthians 15:40).

  • v10 "while you were spittle" — mərāt, as mərāq, spittle, the word of 1 Meqabyan 4:18.

  • vv11–15 the rope of Sheol — The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me (Psalm 18:5). The likeness of a rope that grows with a man from the womb is the book's own.

  • v16 "after it has passed away… sevenfold" — taʾatito wa-wino məsbəʿita; the sense of the clause is uncertain.

  • vv19–21 "your spirits from the winds, your dust from the earth, your flame from the fire" — the parts of the body returning from the four elements, as in 1 Meqabyan 8:6–15.

  • v24 "while you sit on the seat of Moses" — The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat (Matthew 23:2).

  • vv31–33 the womb and the storehouses — vv31 and 32 repeat the same words of the woman and of the earth. The earth shall give back those who are asleep in it… and the chambers shall give back the souls which have been committed to them (2 Esdras 7:32); compare 1 Meqabyan 7:24 and 1 Enoch 51:1.

  • v34 "At the blowing of the horn… in the twinkling of an eye" — in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised (1 Corinthians 15:52).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Day of Judgment
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 15

The Day of God

1Those who held fast to good deeds will rejoice then; but those who grew slack, saying, "The dead will not rise," will grieve then, when they see that they have risen from the dead with their evil deeds that are of no use.

2Their own deeds will judge them; though no one accuses them, they themselves will know how they are judged.

3They will stand in the place of the wicked on the day of weeping and judgment, on the day of punishment, on the day of God,

4on the day of darkness, on the day of gloom, on the day of fog, on the day of ḍaʿāʿ, on the day of lightning,

5on the day of fear and trembling, on the day of sleet and frost, on the day of ice,

6on the day when the evil man is repaid as he did evil, the pure as he did purity, and the harsh as he did robbery,

7when the master is not honored above the slave, nor the mistress above the maidservant,

8when the king is not honored above the poor man, the ruler above the child, the father above his son, or the mother above her daughter,

9when the rich is not honored above the poor, the proud above the humble, or the great above the small. For it is the day of judgment, the day of repayment and of sentence, the day on which each is repaid as he has done,

10the day on which the doers of good are rewarded, and those who did evil are repaid with evil,

11the day when those rewarded with good rejoice and those repaid with evil grieve; and those who made the Scriptures a lie, saying, "The dead will not rise," will see it.

Joy without End and Grief without Comfort

12Then all the sinners of the earth will weep for the sins they did, because grief without comfort has come upon them, because they did no good on the earth.

13So too the joy of the good, who did good, will not end forever and ever; for while they were on the earth they held fast to doing good,

14and did not transgress the commandment of their Creator, for they knew that they would rise from the dead.

15Because they did not transgress His commandment, they will inherit [words lost]

16In the heavens too He gave them as an inheritance the land of life that He swore to their fathers, on the day of the resurrection, when the rich are made poor.

17The doers of evil who did not believe in the resurrection of the dead and the law of God, and did not remember the day of resurrection, will wail.

18Then they will see the evil that comes on them, which has no end, no healing and no comfort; in their hearts grief without comfort, and no rest;

19the worm that does not sleep and the fire that is not quenched;

20and outside their bodies, fire and tay, a stormy wind, ice, hail and sleet raining down on them,

21the lash of fire for those who do not believe in the resurrection of the dead.

Notes

  • v2 "though no one accuses them, they themselves will know" — their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them on that day when… God judges the secrets of men (Romans 2:15–16).

  • vv3–5 "on the day of darkness, on the day of gloom…" — A day of wrath is that day, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness (Zephaniah 1:15). Ḍaʿāʿ is a word not otherwise known; sleet, frost and ice (dadak, marqi, ḥasatyā) are taken as the cold of v20.

  • vv7–9 "the master is not honored above the slave" — it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest; as with the slave, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress (Isaiah 24:2); who shows no partiality to princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor (Job 34:19).

  • v15 "they will inherit [words lost]" — the Ge'ez breaks off at wa-yəwarrəsu, and they will inherit; `SOURCES.md` lists the verse among those cut short.

  • v19 "the worm that does not sleep and the fire that is not quenched" — their worm shall not die, their fire shall not be quenched (Isaiah 66:24; Mark 9:48), as in 1 Meqabyan 12:22.

  • v20 "fire and tay" — a word not otherwise known.
