when the rich is not honored above the poor, the proud above the humble, or the great above the small. For it is the day of judgment, the day of repayment and of sentence, the day on which each is repaid as he has done,
the day on which the doers of good are rewarded, and those who did evil are repaid with evil,
the day when those rewarded with good rejoice and those repaid with evil grieve; and those who made the Scriptures a lie, saying, "The dead will not rise," will see it.
Joy without End and Grief without Comfort
Then all the sinners of the earth will weep for the sins they did, because grief without comfort has come upon them, because they did no good on the earth.
So too the joy of the good, who did good, will not end forever and ever; for while they were on the earth they held fast to doing good,
and did not transgress the commandment of their Creator, for they knew that they would rise from the dead.
Because they did not transgress His commandment, they will inherit [words lost]
In the heavens too He gave them as an inheritance the land of life that He swore to their fathers, on the day of the resurrection, when the rich are made poor.
The doers of evil who did not believe in the resurrection of the dead and the law of God, and did not remember the day of resurrection, will wail.
Then they will see the evil that comes on them, which has no end, no healing and no comfort; in their hearts grief without comfort, and no rest;
the worm that does not sleep and the fire that is not quenched;
and outside their bodies, fire and tay, a stormy wind, ice, hail and sleet raining down on them,
the lash of fire for those who do not believe in the resurrection of the dead.

chapters.title: Nails and Hair
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 16

Your Own Body

1Consider now for yourself what is in your body: the nails of your hands and your feet, and the hair of your head. Each time you cut them, they grow out again. By this know it, if you have understanding and knowledge to believe.

2Where, you say, do these come from, the nails of your hands and your feet and the hair of your head? Is it not God who ordered them to grow? So you may know that the resurrection of the dead will be of your own body, not in another body, so that you may know for yourself that you will rise from the dead.

3You will be repaid according to the deeds you have done, offense and sin, at the resurrection of the dead, because you led the people astray, saying, "There is no resurrection of the dead."

Each Seed of Its Own Kind

4Now you will see it, when the day of your repayment comes. What you sowed does not refuse to sprout, whether grain or wheat.

5Again, the tree you planted does not refuse to sprout, whether vine or fig; its leaves and its fruit do not change.

6If you plant a vine, it does not change into a fig; if you plant a fig, it does not change into a vine; if you sow wheat, it does not change into barley;

7and if you sow barley, it does not change into wheat. Each, by its seed and of its own kind, in its fruit and its wood, its leaves and its sap, receives a blessing by the dew of mercy from God, and brings out fruit.

8So too the earth brings out what God has sown. It makes the soul and body of the doers of good sprout, not changed into doers of evil, and the doers of evil not changed into doers of good; what God has sown sprouts, soul and body.

9When the time comes for the blowing of the horn, the dead will rise by the dew of mercy from God: those who did good, to the resurrection of life, and their reward is the garden of joy, the dwellings for the pure that He prepared for the good, where there is no disease or sickness, where they never die again;

10but those who did evil, to the resurrection of judgment, with the devil who led them astray

11and his evil demons, who do not want a single one of all mankind to be saved, into eternal judgment,

12below, beneath, to the end of darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, where there is no compassion or mercy and no way out forever and ever; for they did no good in their life on the earth while they were in their bodies.

13Because of this they are judged at the resurrection, soul and body.

14Woe to those who do not believe in the resurrection of soul and body together, in which God shows the greatness of His wonders!

15Each one will be repaid according to his deeds and the labor of his hand.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the nails of your hands… the hair of your head" — not a hair of your head will perish (Luke 21:18). The book's likeness: what grows again from the same body shows that the body rises as itself.

  • vv4–7 "a vine… does not change into a fig" — the likeness of 1 Meqabyan 8:29–31. Can a fig tree, my brothers, bear olives, or a grapevine produce figs? (James 3:12); to each kind of seed its own body (1 Corinthians 15:38).

  • vv9–10 "to the resurrection of life… to the resurrection of judgment" — those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment (John 5:29).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Grain and the Vine
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 17

The Grain of Wheat

1A grain of wheat, if it does not die, does not sprout or bear fruit. But if the grain of wheat dies, it makes a root in the earth, puts out leaves, becomes a stalk and bears fruit; and you know

2yourselves that one grain of wheat becomes many grains.

3So this grain sprouts from wind and water and earth, and the sun in place of fire; for without the sun the wheat cannot bear fruit.

4The wind is in place of the soul, and without wind the wheat cannot bear fruit; and the water is what waters it and soaks the earth.

5Once the dust and the earth are soaked, it makes a root and rises up, and bears fruit as much as God has blessed it.

The Vine

6For the grain of wheat is in the likeness of Adam, into whom God's speaking spirit was breathed. The vine too is watered with water; it makes roots and takes up water through the fine cords of its roots,

7and lifts it up above, into the crown of the leaves; for the dew of mercy from God nurses them at the tops of the tall branches. It ripens in the heat of the sun and bears fruit from God.

8It gives a good fragrance that gladdens the heart. When they eat it, it satisfies like water and bread, so that one is not hungry or thirsty; and when they press it, it gives the blood of the cluster.

9When they drink it, it gladdens the heart of man, as it says in the Psalm, "Wine gladdens the heart of man." But a man who takes pleasure in it gets drunk when he opens his mouth and swallows and fills his belly, and his blood is poured into his heart.

10It makes him senseless, for drunkenness with wine makes a man very foolish; it makes the cliffs and ravines seem to him like level ground, and he does not know the stumbling block or the thorn in his hands and his feet.

11So God has done with the vine and its fruit, so that His name may be praised by those who do His will and those who believe in the resurrection of the dead.

12He makes those who believe in the resurrection of the dead rejoice in the dwelling of life.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "A grain of wheat, if it does not die" — unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24).

  • vv3–4 "wind and water and earth, and the sun in place of fire… the wind in place of the soul" — the four parts of 1 Meqabyan 8:6–8 and 2 Meqabyan 14:19, found again in the grain.

  • v6 "God's speaking spirit was breathed" — manfasa ʾƎgziʾabəḥer nababit: the LORD God… breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature (Genesis 2:7).

  • v8 "the blood of the cluster" — you drank foaming wine made from the blood of the grape (Deuteronomy 32:14); he washes… his vesture in the blood of grapes (Genesis 49:11).

  • vv9–10 "Wine gladdens the heart of man… makes the cliffs seem like level ground" — wine to gladden the heart of man (Psalm 104:15); Who has woe?… Those who tarry long over wine… You will be like one who lies down in the midst of the sea (Proverbs 23:29–34).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Where Is the Beauty of the Young
chapters.html:
2 Meqabyan 18

The Error of Those Who Deny

1How great is the error you have fallen into, you who do not believe in the resurrection of the dead! When they take you where you do not know, at that time you will repent where it does you no good, when they cast you into judgment because you did not believe in the resurrection of the dead, in body and soul together.

2You will be rewarded as you have done, whether good or evil; for you harmed the hearts of your companions, saying, "We believe that the dead who have become ashes and earth will not rise."

3Because of this their companions grow foolish; for there is no reprieve from their death and no strength against their punishment, and they are not spared the toil, for they must stand before the judgment seat of God.

4They will be greatly ashamed when He rebukes them in His wrath and is angry with them for all the evil they did; for though they do not know the way of God, they speak, and they themselves do not know where they came from,

5nor do they know where they are going, into the judgment of burning fire. According to the crookedness of their heart they teach their companions, for they are bitter and rough in their deeds and harsh, and they teach a crooked word, saying, "There is no resurrection of the dead."

6On that day they will know that the dead rise, and they will be judged for not believing in the resurrection of the dead, which is for all the creation of mankind.

The Fruit of Adam

7For we are all the fruit of Adam, and because of Adam we died; for because of the error of our father Adam, the judgment of death from God came upon us all.

8Again, so that we may be repaid for what we have done, we will rise with that Adam our father; for by the ignorance of our father Adam he was made subject in the world to death.

9Because of this we were repaid for Adam's transgression: our flesh melted in the grave, and our bones were broken.

10The earth drank our marrow, and it perished; our beauty melted in the dust, our flesh was covered in the earth, and our pleasant voice was covered in the earth.

11The light went out of our bright eyes, and our beauty perished in the tomb and became dust.

12Where is the beauty of the handsome young men, whose stature was lovely and whose voices were sweet? Where is the greatness of the strong?

13Where is the might of kings and the honor of rulers, who rode on horses, adorned themselves with gold and silver, and were armed with gleaming weapons of war?

14Where is the sweetness of food, and of sweet wine?

Notes

  • v7 "we are all the fruit of Adam, and because of Adam we died" — as in Adam all die, so also in Christ shall all be made alive (1 Corinthians 15:22); sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin (Romans 5:12).

  • v11 "The light went out of our bright eyes" — the Ge'ez has ʿəda, a word not otherwise known in this place; the light is the plain sense with bright eyes.

  • vv12–14 "Where is the beauty… Where is the might of kings" — Where are the princes of the nations, and those who rule over the beasts on earth… those who heap up silver and gold?… They have vanished and gone down to Hades (Baruch 3:16–19).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
